title: Renovate regression-runner adapters and decouple workload profiling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Our regression runner (the process that executes the perf regression suite and emits canonical metrics) has accreted three adapter layers over the last 18 months. Those adapters (legacy load adapter, new streaming adapter, and the eval-proxy shim) currently share responsibilities for request shaping, warmup sequencing, and metric tagging. This has led to flaky runs, duplicated metric transformations, and frequent CI overhead when updating model variants or sequence-length profiles.

Goal: Refactor the regression-runner adapter surface to a clear adapter contract: (1) separate workload profiling (sampling and input shaping) from request emission; (2) standardize metric tags and schema at the runner boundary; (3) remove duplicate code paths so new adapters can be registered without touching core orchestration. Outcome should be more stable CI runs, 30% reduction in flaky job restarts, and simpler onboarding for new load adapters.

Scope:
- Introduce a WorkloadProfile interface that lives in perf-core and owns sequence-length distributions, tokenization hints, and warmup policies.
- Extract all sampling logic from legacy adapter into a single impl under perf-core; adapters will only consume WorkloadProfile outputs.
- Consolidate metric tagging and export at runner boundary (prometheus + structured logs).
- Provide compatibility layer for the streaming adapter for a 2-cycle migration.
- Add unit + integration tests that simulate mixed adapter runs.

Out of scope: full rewrite of the streaming adapter internals, changes to production traffic routing, or runtime kernel selection logic.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Regression CI runs for perf-regression-master succeed under the new runner in 95% of scheduled runs over a 2-week observation window.
2) No change in emitted metric names; tags are standardized and documented.
3) New WorkloadProfile is covered by unit tests (>=90% branch coverage) and a small integration test that verifies warmup sequences for 3 canonical profiles (short/medium/long).
4) Migration guide and code examples added to the perf-platform docs (Confluence link below).

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We prefer moving sampling logic into perf-core to avoid duplicate bug fixes across adapters. Trade-off: perf-core becomes slightly larger and requires more deliberate backward compatibility.
- Two-stage migration chosen to minimize blast radius: step 1 (this ticket) erects the adapter contract and moves sampling; step 2 (follow-up) will remove legacy hooks from adapters once all consumers migrate.
- We will not attempt runtime performance micro-optimizations in this ticket; those will be handled after functional stability is achieved.

Tasks:
- [ ] Design WorkloadProfile interface and doc the contract (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/perf-core/pull/488)
- [ ] Implement sampling extraction and wire into regression runner (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/regression-runner/pull/162)
- [ ] Add integration tests and flakiness detector in CI (flake rate baseline: 12% -> target <=3%)
- [ ] Update perf-platform Confluence page with migration guide (https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PERF/pages/823412/Regression+Runner+Adapter+Migration)
- [ ] Run a canary in staging for 3 days and collect run stability metrics

Monitoring and rollout:
- Canary in staging cluster 'perf-stage-01' for 72 hours observing run_success_rate, mean_run_duration, and token_emission_rate.
- If run_success_rate < 95% after 72h, rollback plan: revert regression-runner change and open follow-up triage ticket.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cPerfProfileDesign/view (internal)
- PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/perf-core/pull/488, github.com/redwood-inference/regression-runner/pull/162
- Confluence migration guide: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PERF/pages/823412/Regression+Runner+Adapter+Migration
- Benchmark dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runner-staging/perf-regression

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle metric tag normalization can break downstream alert queries. Mitigation: keep old metric names for two cycles and provide alias shim.
- Risk: increased perf-core surface area slows future releases. Mitigation: keep the interface minimal and add a deprecation policy for any new methods.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-45120: Remove legacy adapter hooks once all teams complete migration (estimate 5 points).
- ENG-45200: Optimize sampling hot path for micro-benchmarks (post-migration).
